title: Minneapolis: the Pettiford family and Adolphus Alsbrook
summary: With the bassist he goes to Minneapolis, finds an after-hours joint, meets Oscar Pettiford, the Pettiford family and bassist Adolphus Alsbrook, and gets a job in St. Paul.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. So pretty soon that job run out. And we said, "Where should we go from here, Bassy and I?" I said, "Well, let's go to Minneapolis.
Yeah. I said, "Let's go to Minneapolis." So we had enough bus fare to get...
Were these all like the first time you had been to any of these places?
Yeah, first time, you know. So I didn't really know what to do in Minneapolis. I guess God was looking out for me...
But I guess that was the biggest city you had been to.

Yeah, it was the biggest city that I had been to besides Denver and Albuquerque, and they wasn't no big cities really. So I went to Minneapolis. And just by chance, it was on a Sunday, and I went into this after-hours

joint -- they had after-hours joints I'd play. And that's where I met Oscar Pettiford and the Pettiford Family, the brothers and... Let me see, who else did I meet up there? That bass player, a helluva bass player. Adolphus...
I can never get whether it's Alsbrook or Allbrook...
Milt Hinton has talked about him quite a bit.

Yeah, I met him out there. And luckily, I met a piano player up there who was looking for a trumpet player, so he asked me was I working, and I said, "You got a job?" He said, "Yeah." I said, "Well, I am now. Well, what it is." So he was working in St. Paul. Anyway, I went over to St. Paul to work for him, and thank goodness, because it was colder than a son-of-a-bitch. You talk about cold, boy, St. Paul and Minneapolis was out of sight.
